findings.area: Acceptance criterion 5 (cursor advance rule): Overflow/Stopped stop the run and advance only the covered prefix
findings.summary: The service's enqueue-returned Stopped stop path is not exercised by any test; only the Overflow stop (and the separate lifecycle-fence stop) is tested.
findings.detail: LibraryReconciliationService.cs:253-260 stops a cursor-governed run when the enqueue outcome is Overflow OR Stopped, and maps Stopped to LibraryReconciliationOutcome.Fenced (lines 283-290). The worker report's acceptance-criteria item 5 claims the tests establish 'Overflow/Stopped stop the run and the cursor advances only over the covered prefix' and cites ReconciliationCursorResumeTests.OverflowStopsAtTheFirstUncoveredItemAndAdvancesTheCursorOnlyOverTheCoveredPrefix, CancellationAdvancesTheCursorOnlyOverTheCoveredPrefix, and FenceStopAdvancesTheCursorOnlyOverTheCoveredPrefix. None of those exercises a sink returning WorkHintEnqueueOutcome.Stopped: the OutcomeOverride scripts use only Accepted/Coalesced/InFlight/Overflow (ReconciliationCursorResumeTests.cs:194-195, 231-236, 259-260, 402-403), and a repository-wide test search for WorkHintEnqueueOutcome.Stopped finds only LibraryWorkQueueTests.cs (the queue vocabulary), not the service. FenceStopAdvances... stops via AllowsNewWork() (the lifecycle fence), which is a different code path from the sink's Stopped return (LibraryWorkQueue returns Stopped only when its own _accepting==0 on shutdown, or for a malformed hint; a raised fence does not make the queue return Stopped). Consequence: deleting the 'or WorkHintEnqueueOutcome.Stopped' clause, or mis-handling the Stopped classification (e.g. covering the stopped item and continuing to wrap the cursor past it, exactly the class of defect probe P11 targeted), would leave the whole suite green. The production code is correct as written; the evidence for this named sub-behavior is missing, so the report's claim for criterion 5 is not fully established.
evidence: src/ArrTags/Reconciliation/LibraryReconciliationService.cs:253-260 (usesCursor && outcome is Overflow or Stopped -> stopOutcome/break)
src/ArrTags/Reconciliation/LibraryReconciliationService.cs:271-290 (Stopped -> LibraryReconciliationOutcome.Fenced, cursor advanced over covered prefix)
tests/ArrTags.Tests/ReconciliationCursorResumeTests.cs:313-339 (FenceStop uses the lifecycle fence via AllowsNewWork, not the sink's Stopped return)
findings.recommended_action: Add one ReconciliationCursorResumeTests fact that scripts the sink to return WorkHintEnqueueOutcome.Stopped for a mid-scope item and asserts: outcome Fenced, the stopped item is not counted as Covered, the cursor is the last covered item (not the stopped item), and the following run resumes at the stopped item. No production change is required.

findings.summary: The reconciliation cursor is a Cache record that is not exempt from the render-cache TTL/quota retention, unlike MetadataStateStore, so it can be pruned between whole-scope runs and silently reset coverage.
findings.detail: ReconciliationCursorStore writes under StateAuthority.Cache (ReconciliationCursorStore.cs:132). StateRetentionService.RunRetentionPass exempts only MetadataStateStore.RecordKind (StateRetentionService.cs:147); StateRetention.ApplyCacheRetention then deletes every non-exempt cache *.json older than RenderCacheTtlMinutes (StateRetention.cs:45-63). The cursor is the only non-exempt Cache record (grep for StateAuthority.Cache: MetadataStateStore and ReconciliationCursorStore), so quota eviction is not a practical threat, but age pruning is: the default TTL is 24h (OperationalLimits.cs:131) versus the default 12h scheduled interval (ArrTagsReconciliationTask.cs:42), so under defaults the cursor's mtime is refreshed before expiry and it survives. If the effective whole-scope interval exceeds the configured TTL (a user-configurable Jellyfin interval; TTL floor 1 minute), the cursor is pruned and every cycle restarts from the beginning, which is the F4 behavior the mechanism exists to remove. This is consistent with the ADR's Cache-authority 'missing resets to the start' semantics and is default-safe, so it is recorded rather than blocking 19.1; it is an integration interaction not covered by the 19.1 acceptance criteria and belongs to the 19.2/19.5 coverage and integration verification.
evidence: src/ArrTags/State/StateRetention.cs:45-63 (age TTL deletion of non-exempt cache records)
findings.recommended_action: Consider adding ReconciliationCursorStore.RecordKind to the exemptCacheKinds list (or documenting the TTL-vs-interval interaction as a registered limitation) in task 19.5; no action required for 19.1.

findings.area: Concurrency / state consistency of the persisted cursor
findings.summary: Reviewed overlapping whole-scope runs: each run writes only a position it actually covered after reading its own starting cursor, so concurrency can cause a bounded re-cover (last writer moves the cursor back) but cannot skip an uncovered item.
findings.detail: LibraryReconciliationService is a singleton with no cross-run lock, and a manual/periodic scheduled run can overlap a post-scan run. Each run reads the cursor once at start (line 170), resumes from it, and persists only the position of the last item that run covered (AdvanceCursor, lines 418-437). If run A (from X) and run B (from X) overlap, whichever finishes last writes a position it covered, so the cursor can move back to an earlier covered position but never forward past an item either run did not cover; the next run re-covers the overlap. No skip is possible, so this is a bounded extra-work effect, not a state-integrity failure. No change is required; recorded for the audit trail.
